decks.name: LeetCode #146 - LRU Cache
decks.description: Design and implement a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache data structure

cards.question: LRU Cache: Design a data structure that follows the constraints of a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache. Implement the LRUCache class with methods: LRUCache(int capacity) initializes the LRU cache with positive size capacity, int get(int key) returns the value of the key if the key exists, otherwise returns -1, and void put(int key, int value) updates the value of the key if the key exists, otherwise adds the key-value pair to the cache. If the number of keys exceeds the capacity from this operation, evict the least recently used key. The functions get and put must each run in O(1) average time complexity.

solutions.name: Brute Force
solutions.explanation: Use a list to track order of usage and a dictionary for fast value lookup. On get/put operations, remove and re-append the key to mark it as recently used. When capacity is exceeded, remove the first element (least recently used). Simple but O(n) operations due to list manipulation.

solutions.name: Doubly Linked List
solutions.explanation: Use hash map for O(1) key lookup combined with doubly linked list for O(1) insertion/deletion. Each node stores key-value pair with prev/next pointers. Maintain dummy head and tail nodes to simplify edge cases. On access, move node to tail (most recent). On eviction, remove node at head.next (least recent). Most efficient solution with true O(1) operations.

solutions.name: Built-In Data Structure
solutions.explanation: Use OrderedDict in Python which maintains insertion order and provides O(1) operations. Move accessed keys to end using move_to_end or delete+reinsert. When capacity exceeded, use popitem(last=False) to remove oldest entry. Leverages language-specific optimized data structure for clean implementation.
